nextStoryContext:
Closed the reviewer-filed WARNING (install.sh:107): the fourth error branch of the SHA256SUMS.txt verification block (`EXPECTED_HASH="$(grep -F "  ${ASSET}" "${TMP_SUMS}" | awk '{print $1}')" || true` followed by `-z EXPECTED_HASH`) had no committed test, even though US-004 pinned the other three legs (mismatch, unreachable manifest, no hash tool). Added a fourth `writeFakeCurl` behavior, 'no-checksum-entry', to test/install-sh.test.ts: the SHA256SUMS.txt call still succeeds (curl exit 0, manifest reachable) but the single line it writes names a fixed, deliberately-wrong asset (`gateship-unrelated-asset`) instead of `${ASSET_NAME}` read back from `.checksum-state`, so install.sh's own `grep -F "  ${ASSET}"` against the real per-host asset name finds zero matches regardless of which os/arch the test runs on. New test asserts all three: exitCode===1, stderr contains the exact `ERROR: no checksum entry for ${assetNameForHost()}` diagnostic (host-specific asset name, matching install.sh's exact wording verbatim, not a substring guess), and `readdirSync(installDir)` is empty (nothing was ever installed). Ran the new test standalone (8/8 pass including the 7 pre-existing legs) before running the full spine.

NOTE on test-suite investigation (transparency, not a blocker): a single early `bun test` invocation, captured through `| tail -30` (which destroys all output before the last 30 lines), reported '6001 pass / 1 fail' with no visible identification of which test failed or why (the failure detail was upstream of the tail window and is unrecoverable). Per the no-flaky-evasion rule I did not just re-run-and-shrug; I re-ran the FULL suite four more times with untruncated output captured to a file (two standalone `bun test` runs, plus two full `bun run check:all` runs, each ~148-153s), and every one of those four came back deterministically clean: 6002 pass / 0 fail, all `check:all` sub-gates 'ok' (typecheck, test w/ coverage report all green, embed-vendor, lint, file-size, debt-markers, version-skips, coverage, dead-code, dup, ci-parity, agents-md, test-sleeps, skip-ratchet), exit code 0 both times. My diff touches only test/install-sh.test.ts (a self-contained shell-shim test file whose new leg runs in isolation with its own mkdtempSync dirs, cleaned up in afterEach), which is not plausibly the source of an unrelated single-run flake elsewhere in a 6002-test suite; the standalone install-sh.test.ts run alone was clean 8/8 twice. Given the specific failing test could not be identified (my own tooling mistake truncating the capture, not suite nondeterminism I could pin down) and four full clean reproductions followed, I proceeded rather than block on an unreproducible, unidentifiable single data point — flagging this transparently rather than silently re-running past it. If this recurs for the next story, capture full untruncated `bun test` output (never pipe through `tail`) so the specific failing test and its stack trace survive for triage.

prd.json also carries a pre-existing (not authored by me) reviewer-filed diff from before this session started: this story (US-R1-001) and a sibling (US-R1-002, release.yml guard for the attest/SHA256SUMS.txt step, still passes:false) were appended as new stories with priorities 1-2, the five US-00X stories were renumbered priority 3-7, and a `review` block (roundsCompleted:1, lastVerdict:'FIXES_PENDING:2', 5 findings) was added recording the review round that filed both new stories plus 3 non-blocking SUGGESTION/consider-class findings. Committed unmodified alongside my own test file per the 'commit ALL changes' instruction; I did not touch its content. US-R1-002 (release.yml static guard, priority 2, requires:none) is the next likely dispatch target and is unrelated to install.sh.
